Add slow processes that drive a model's latent processes

Source: R/ctModelSlowComponent.R
ctModelSlowComponent.Rd

Each latent in indices gets a slow latent, named slow_ and the latent's name, that drives it through the drift. An estimated effect DRIFT[k, slow_k] shifts the level the latent returns to with the slow process, so a process can drift over weeks while fluctuating over hours. The latent's equilibrium is DRIFT[k, slow_k] / |DRIFT[k, k]| times the slow process, so a person with faster dynamics follows the slow process less closely.

Usage

ctModelSlowComponent(ctm, indices = seq_len(ctm$n.latent))

Arguments

ctm

A model from ctModel(type = 'ct').

indices

Which latents get a slow process, by position.

Value

The extended model.

Details

The slow process is always slower than the latent it drives. Its drift is the latent's drift times inv_logit(r), with r a PARS parameter named drift_ and the slow process's name. If both rates were free, they could swap, since with only the latent measured the two processes are interchangeable. The latent's drift parameter is declared in PARS for this, keeping its name, transform, individual variation and predictor effects, so where the latent's rate varies over people the slow process's rate varies with it. Where the latent's drift is fixed, the slow process's drift is a fraction of that value. Where the latent's drift is an expression, the slow process's persistence is left free.

A slow process has innovations of unit variance (the effect carries its scale), correlated with those of other slow processes, including ones added earlier, and uncorrelated with the others. It has no loadings, no intercept, and no individual variation or predictor effects. Its initial mean and variance are its stationary ones (T0MEANS and the T0VAR diagonal 'stationary', see ctFit), zero and 1 / (2 |a|) for persistence a. Its initial covariance with the latent it drives is free, and with other states zero.

The effect needs a starting value away from zero, because at zero neither the slow process nor its effect has a gradient. When refitting from a model without the slow process, start the effect at one (either sign) and the fraction small. ctModelImprove starts it at a tenth.

See also

ctModelHigherOrder for the other structural extension the search tries.

Examples

m <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'),
  latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'), LAMBDA = diag(2))
m2 <- ctModelSlowComponent(m, 1:2)
m2$latentNames
p <- m2$pars
p[p$matrix %in% c('DRIFT', 'DIFFUSION') & (p$row > 2 | p$col > 2) &
  (!is.na(p$param) | p$value != 0), c('matrix', 'row', 'col', 'param', 'value')]
